posts.name: Justin Koh
posts.cooked:
Verify files

First verify the evolution packages, in case some files are modified/damaged:

$ rpm -Va 'evolution*'

Install evolution?

This is just a wild guess—maybe evolution-alarm-notify requires something from the evolution client package to work correctly (like some gsettings schema, or this file /usr/lib64/evolution-data-server/ui-modules/module-evolution-alarm-notify.so).

You could try installing evolution and see if evolution-alarm-notify stops crashing.

For reference, this is what I have installed. I use Evolution client on F37 Xfce without this issue.

$ rpm -qa 'evolution*'
evolution-data-server-langpacks-3.46.4-1.fc37.noarch
evolution-data-server-3.46.4-1.fc37.x86_64
evolution-langpacks-3.46.4-1.fc37.noarch
evolution-3.46.4-1.fc37.x86_64

Workaround: disable evolution-alarm-notify

Do you actually need evolution-alarm-notify? It is the program that shows this type of pop-up:

screenshot_2023-03-11_17-59-31210×314 12.2 KB

I don’t know if GNOME components like Calendar use evolution-alarm-notify or their own notifications.

It runs via an autostart file (/etc/xdg/autostart/org.gnome.Evolution-alarm-notify.desktop) that is installed with evolution-data-server.

So, if you don’t need it, you could disable the autostart by making a file with the same name in ~/.config/autostart and setting Hidden=true, like this:

$ printf '[Desktop Entry]\nHidden=true\n' > ~/.config/autostart/org.gnome.Evolution-alarm-notify.desktop

This doesn’t solve the crash, but stops it from running on every login.
